We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 139.25, 134.60, 129.00, 129.00, 128.30, 128.30, 49.40, 26.10, 11.40 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups in the compound. Methyl carbon typically appears around 10-15 ppm for aliphatic CH3 attached to carbon (e.g., methyl of alkane). Also 20-30 ppm for CH3 attached to heteroatoms or aromatic? 26.10 could be CH3 attached to something else (maybe isopropyl). 11.40 is typical for a terminal methyl (e.g., CH3-CH2-). 49.40 could be a carbon attached to heteroatom (e.g., O-CH3). But O-CH3 appears around 55 ppm. 49.4 could be a CH (maybe CH attached to aromatic). So we need count of CH3 groups. In carbon NMR, each distinct carbon gives a signal. We have signals at 11.40 (likely CH3), 26.10 (could be CH3), maybe also 49.40 (could be CH3 attached to heteroatom? but typical OCH3 ~55, NCH3 ~30-40). 49.4 maybe a CH2? Not sure.

We could also get proton NMR to confirm. Let's request proton NMR.
